blocks.heading: The visual-atlas product scans a repo, maps its domains, and renders a navigable tree of orientation pages and focused technical topics.

rows.value: The atlas **block model**, the `atlas.domains.json` domain/topic hierarchy, deterministic page paths and navigation, mechanical drafts, self-contained rendering, and completeness checks.

A standing onboarding-to-reference map: system and domain pages orient the reader, while recursively nested topic pages explain mechanisms without overloading their parents. Mechanical scan handles inventory; a human authors the hierarchy and meaning.
The page you are reading **is** this domain. The very generator documented below produced it — the scanner drafted these cards, then a human enriched them.

bigIdea.label: The load-bearing idea
bigIdea.line: "Hybrid — the scanner does the inventory, the human writes the domains and the why."
bigIdea.sub: `scanInventory` finds modules, imports, and exports; `reconcile` maintains domain coverage; `buildPageTree` derives stable recursive paths and navigation; and the draft builders emit system, domain, and topic skeletons. The scanner never reorganizes the authored hierarchy.

blocks.title: The pieces
blocks.intro: One CLI over six library modules: grouping and page-tree configuration, scanning and drafts, the block model, self-contained rendering, and quality checks for page structure, readability, current truth, and freshness.

cards.name: CLI
cards.purpose: `bin/atlas.ts` — full scan, single-domain subtree refresh, and render-only modes. It walks configured page nodes, writes recursive topic drafts, derives navigation at render time, and keeps each nested page's sidecars in its own folder.

cards.name: config + page tree
cards.purpose: `atlas-config.ts` owns domain grouping plus authored recursive topic types. `atlas-tree.ts` derives stable page paths, breadcrumbs, relationships, owner-scoped landing-page reading paths, and labeled file-level evidence scopes without changing the authored hierarchy.

cards.name: scan + draft
cards.purpose: `gather-atlas.ts` — walks srcRoots, parses imports/exports/routers per module, aggregates cross-domain edges, and emits the atlas + domain draft documents (with the mechanical domain-map diagram).

cards.name: block model
cards.purpose: `atlas-blocks.ts` — system/domain/topic blocks plus `PageNavigation` and page options. Topic leads, flows, rules, and collapsed implementation references share the existing diagram and example primitives.

cards.name: render
cards.purpose: `assemble-atlas.ts` — renders system, domain, and topic pages in one self-contained shell. It adds breadcrumbs, current-branch navigation, child cards, owner-scoped reading paths on landing pages, related-page navigation, offline structured search, and collapsed implementation references.

cards.name: quality checks
cards.purpose: `lint-atlas.ts` keeps page-shape, density, paragraph length, card size, project-history, and topic-extraction warnings visible during rendering. The emitted checker separately enforces safe paths, live domain membership, page identity, evidence-scoped grounding, links, and per-page freshness.

blocks.title: How a full scan runs
blocks.intro: A full scan reconciles domain coverage, derives the authored page tree, and emits system, domain, and topic drafts only when absent. Rendering then adds navigation from the tree rather than copying it into authored JSON. A single-domain refresh regenerates that domain's complete configured subtree.

diagram.caption: Drift is **reported, never applied** — the human edits `atlas.domains.json` globs to resolve it.

blocks.title: The pieces, in depth
blocks.intro: A full section per piece — what it does, how it works, its files and exports, and how it connects to the rest of the toolkit.

components.name: CLI
detail: The single entry point has three modes. **Full scan** reconciles domain coverage, validates the configured page tree, emits missing system/domain/topic drafts, and renders every configured page. **Single-domain** regenerates the selected domain plus every nested topic beneath it. **Render-only** replays committed JSON with navigation and page identity derived from the adjacent config; when output differs from source, it carries that config into the output so the emitted checker remains usable.

`writeDraftIfAbsent` is the no-clobber guarantee for full scans; `--force` requests clean replacement. `listDocJsons` follows configuration order when a tree exists and recursively discovers standalone page JSON otherwise. `renderFile` handles `atlas`, `domain`, and `topic` documents and passes derived navigation into the shared assembler.

components.name: config + page tree
detail: `atlas.domains.json` is the human-owned source of truth: each `DomainConfig` carries a `slug`, `name`, and `globs` for source ownership, while optional recursive `topics` describe the reader's conceptual page tree. `firstGuessConfig` seeds domains; `reconcile` refills each domain's `modules` while preserving authored purposes, topics, source groups, and reading paths.

`atlas-tree.ts` turns the authored hierarchy into deterministic page identities, safe nested output paths, breadcrumbs, parent/child relationships, owner-scoped reading paths, and related-page validation. Topic `sources` are labeled include/exclude glob groups: they may overlap and span folders because they identify evidence, not ownership. `resolveTopicSources` fingerprints at file granularity. Drift remains explicit: `reconcile` reports unassigned modules, stale paths, and empty domains without reorganizing pages.

components.name: scan + draft
detail: The hub of the [full-scan flow](#arch). `scanInventory` walks the srcRoots, and per module records resolved in-repo import keys, exported names, and whether it is a tRPC router — skipping generated/test trees and co-located `*.test`/`*.spec` files. It also collects Prisma model names. `aggregateDomainEdges` rolls module→module imports up to cross-domain slug→slug edges (intra-domain edges dropped).

`buildAtlasDraft` emits the system map and uses configured domain purposes. `buildDomainDraft` keeps the legacy deep inventory for domains without child topics, but produces a smaller orientation landing with a collapsed implementation reference when children exist. `buildTopicDraft` creates a plain lead, structured flow and rule sections, and labeled file groups from resolved evidence. The scanner supplies structure and inventory, not the technical explanation.

components.name: block model
detail: The type backbone covers system and domain blocks plus four topic-oriented blocks: `topic-tldr`, `topic-flow`, `topic-rules`, and `implementation-reference`. `PageNavigation` carries derived breadcrumbs, the expanded branch, parent/child/sibling/related links, reading paths, and structured search entries. `TopicOpts` supplies topic shape and direct-entry context to the shared shell.

Beyond the types it carries page-option shapes (`AtlasOpts`/`DomainOpts`), `LAYER_DOTS` (the layer → fill;stroke color table), and small helpers: `collectAtlasDiagrams` pulls every rendered diagram in document order, `assertUniqueAtlasIds` enforces unique block/component/diagram ids, and `isAtlasChapter`/`atlasChapterLabel` drive the numbered chapter nav.

components.name: render
detail: `assembleAtlas`, `assembleDomain`, and `assembleTopic` share one self-contained app shell and block dispatcher. Topic pages render plain leads, ordered flows, guarantees/failure behavior, and closed implementation-reference drawers. With derived navigation, the shell adds breadcrumbs, the current branch, child cards, owner-scoped reading paths on system/domain landings, nearby-page links, and a compact embedded search index.

Search indexes structured titles, purposes, aliases, breadcrumbs, and source paths—not every prose token. `atlas-navigation.js` filters that embedded data locally and creates safe result elements. All page kinds retain the same diagram, example, responsive-shell, and theme behavior.

components.name: quality checks
detail: `lintAtlas`, `lintDomain`, and `lintTopic` enforce the structural floor for their page kinds. A domain with child topics is orientation-first and does not need an expanded components/depth inventory; a topic needs a plain lead, ordered flow, and explicit guarantees/failure behavior.

`lintReadability` measures authored visible prose while excluding diagram source, code HTML, and collapsed implementation-file details. It warns on project-history language, long paragraphs or cards, oversized pages, and multiple independent flows.

The emitted checker keeps readability findings advisory while failing unsafe or contradictory page structure, domain inventory drift derived from live globs, broken links, stale derived counts, and structured references outside a page's evidence.

Each topic fingerprint covers its own config and evidence plus immediate child summaries, so deeper descendants remain independently reviewable. Stamp mode refuses all writes until structural paths and scopes are safe.

blocks.title: Data it owns
blocks.intro: Atlas owns the page block model and the grouping config — the two contracts every atlas page is built from. The block types below are the shape of a page; `AtlasConfig`/`atlas.domains.json` is the human-owned grouping.

rows.name: domain-tldr · components · depth · owns · seams
rows.desc: The domain-page blocks: the lead, the component cards, the in-depth sections, the data-owned table (this block), and the neighbor seams.

rows.name: diagram-section · example
rows.desc: Shared chapter blocks usable on either page type: `diagram-section` (the atlas spine/map and a domain page's internal-arch) and `example` (a worked-example chapter, re-exported from core).

rows.name: Inventory · ModuleInfo · Drift
rows.desc: The mechanical scan products: per-module imports/exports/router flags, Prisma models, and the reported config drift.

blocks.note: The block model lives in `atlas-blocks.ts`; domain/topic/source types live in `atlas-config.ts`, and `atlas-tree.ts` derives navigation and evidence. The scanner fills `modules` and draft skeletons; a human owns grouping, page hierarchy, purpose, and detail.

blocks.title: Seams
blocks.intro: Exposes the atlas CLI and its block model; depends on the rest of the toolkit for parsing, rendering, diagrams, and the shared app-shell.

blocks.note: `gather-atlas` imports **code-intel** (`imports`/`dep-graph`/`trpc-parse`/`prisma-schema`) for the scan; `atlas-blocks` builds on **core**'s `DiagramBlock`/`DiagramKind`; `assemble-atlas` renders via **diagrams** and reuses the **recap** review app-shell + `review.css`. The dependency on the rest of the toolkit is by reuse, not control — atlas stays the driver.
